description: NVIDIA System Management (NVSM) provides cluster-wide health monitoring and diagnostics for DGX systems, covering GPUs, NVLink, InfiniBand, storage, and chassis sensors from a single interactive shell or one-shot command. NVSM aggregates per-component health checks into a single pass/fail rollup and can produce a diagnostic tarball for support tickets.

installation.notes: Ships preinstalled on DGX OS. Requires the nvsm-core service to be running and typically requires root/sudo privileges to run.

global_options.description: Display usage information and available commands

subcommands.name: show
subcommands.description: Show properties, targets, and verbs for the current or specified target in the NVSM address hierarchy (e.g. /systems/localhost, /systems/localhost/gpus/GPU0).

options.description: Show every individual health check instead of a truncated summary list

subcommands.name: dump
subcommands.description: Generate a diagnostic tarball capturing the current health report, suitable for attaching to an NVIDIA support ticket.

subcommands.name: cd
subcommands.description: Change the current working target (CWT) within the NVSM address hierarchy. Interactive-shell only.

output_formats.default: Human-readable text: dot-leader-formatted health check lines ("description....... Status") in one-shot mode, or a Properties/Targets/Verbs listing when navigating the address hierarchy in the interactive shell.

exit_codes.meaning: Success - command completed, though individual health checks may report Warning or Critical status in the output
Error - unknown command/target, invalid path, or the nvsm-core daemon is unreachable

common_usage_patterns.output_example:
Checks
------
Verify installed DIMM memory sticks.......................... Healthy
Number of logical CPU cores................................... Healthy
GPU link speed [0000:39:00.0].................................. Healthy
...

Health Summary
--------------
42 out of 42 checks are Healthy
Overall system status is Healthy
(same format as 'show health', with every check listed instead of the first 20)

common_usage_patterns.description: Generate a diagnostic tarball for a support ticket

error_messages.message: Error: Cannot connect to NVSM daemon. Is nvsm-core service running?
error_messages.meaning: The nvsm-core background service isn't running or isn't reachable
error_messages.resolution: Check the service with 'sudo systemctl status nvsm-core' and start it with 'sudo systemctl start nvsm-core' if it's down.

error_messages.meaning: A 'cd' or path-based command referenced an address that isn't in the NVSM hierarchy
error_messages.resolution: Run 'show' with no arguments at the current target to list valid child targets, then 'cd' into one of those.

interoperability.notes: NVSM's health rollup surfaces the same underlying GPU/NVLink/InfiniBand state that nvidia-smi and dcgmi report individually — an XID error or thermal fault visible in nvidia-smi will also show up as a failing NVSM health check. NVSM is scoped to a single DGX node; bcm handles fleet-wide/cluster-level management.

permissions.read_operations: Requires root/sudo for both interactive and one-shot invocations, per NVIDIA's documented usage.
permissions.write_operations: None — nvsm in this simulator is read-only (health reporting and diagnostic dump); it does not modify GPU or system configuration.

limitations: Requires the nvsm-core service to be running
Scoped to the local DGX node only — no cluster-wide fleet view (use bcm for that)
'show health' without --detailed truncates the check list; use --detailed for the full report
